description: Stop doing legs wrong: skipped days, quarter squats and soreness chasing. Retest your leg-to-waist ratio, then train your leg muscle signals instead with full range, single-leg work and twice-a-week frequency.

scenes.narration: Tape measure. | Thigh, biggest point. | Waist, navel level. | Divide thigh by waist. | That ratio is yours. | Write both numbers down. | The old way built it. | Skipped days, shallow squats. | Done right rebuilds it. | At the end | I tell you | the whole new system. | Your base is waiting. | Same spots, same morning. | The tape keeps receipts.

scenes.label: THE LINE THE OLD WAY NEVER REACHES
scenes.narration: The line is zero point eight zero, thigh to waist, where the frame stands up and the silhouette balances. Under zero point seven two is the old way's signature: legs as the optional session, depth as a rumor, calves as an afterthought. Done right is a specific replacement, not a motivational poster: full range, single-leg work, calves trained like they matter, twice a week on anchors, progressed in ink. It asks less total suffering than the old way's one weekly destruction and delivers more signal, because signal is a product of range, frequency and honesty, not of how destroyed you feel on the stairs. Keep your ratio in front of you. By the verdict you will know exactly which parts of the old way wrote it.
scenes.sub: under 0.72: old way - over 0.88: base built

beats.text: TWICE A WEEK KEEPS IT WARM
HALF THE BODY, TWICE THE RESPECT

scenes.narration: Training leg muscle signals instead of doing leg exercises rests on two pillars: range and frequency. Range is addressing. A squat taken through the full depth you own sends the build order to the quads, glutes and hamstrings as one department; a quarter squat mails it to a fraction of the quad and wonders why the leg looks unfinished. Frequency is coverage. The signal from a leg session fades in days like every other signal, so the biggest muscles you own deserve the same twice-weekly rhythm as everything else, not a weekly ceremony followed by six days of silence. Put the pillars together and done right is almost boring to describe: full-range squats and split squats, calves under stretch and load, twice a week, progressed slowly, forever. The old way was exciting and theatrical. Done right is a postal service: the orders arrive complete, at the right address, on schedule. One more addressing detail for the squat itself. Let the knees travel and the hips sit between the heels, and the load shares across the whole leg the way the anatomy intended. A squat performed as a hinge with barely bent knees mails the order to the lower back instead. Done right is not a depth contest. It is a routing decision, made on every rep, about which muscles receive the signal you are paying for.

beats.text: DAY A: SQUAT + CALVES. DAY B: SPLIT + CALVES.

scenes.narration: The week, concretely. Session A: squats through full range, then calf raises with a pause in the stretch. Session B: split squats, each leg earning its own order with no partner to hide behind, then calf work again, because calves are the slowest responders you own and frequency is their only language. Keep two reps in the tank on everything, so session B survives session A, and progress one variable a week in the log: a rep, a centimeter of depth, a slower negative. Compare the honest arithmetic with the old way: two complete deliveries a week against one theatrical destruction followed by a limp and a skipped session. Your legs hold half your muscle. Done right treats them like the headquarters they are, with regular hours and full deliveries, instead of a festival twice a month. And the calf prescription has a footnote for the impatient: the calf is two muscles wearing one name, and the bent-knee variation reaches the deeper one that straight-knee work misses. Alternate the two across your two weekly sessions and the whole unit develops, front of the mirror and back of the leg alike. Completeness is a signal property too.

beats.text: GENETICS SET THE SHAPE, NOT THE SIZE

scenes.narration: Calves deserve their own scene because done right refuses the genetics excuse in its lazy form. Your calf shape, where the muscle belly sits, is inherited and fixed. Your calf size is not: it responds to the same signals as everything else, just on a slower clock, months instead of weeks, which is exactly why it exposes who is actually patient. The recipe is unglamorous: full stretch under load, a pause at the bottom, high reps some days and heavy reps others, twice a week without exception. The light frame helps here too, because your calf work can ride along on leg days and step days without taxing recovery the way a heavy man's does. Six months of this and the most stubborn muscle on your body files a different report. The men who say calves never grow are almost always men who trained them for six weeks, twice. Done right trains them for six months, always.

beats.text: THE WEAK SIDE SETS THE LOAD
BALANCE IS A SAFETY SIGNAL TOO

scenes.narration: Single-leg work is the truth serum of the done-right system, and it deserves the spotlight before the plan. In every two-legged lift, your strong side quietly donates to your weak side, and the donation is invisible until one thigh measures smaller and one knee starts filing complaints. Split squats end the charity: each leg lifts its own body, at its own level, and the weak side finally receives a full order addressed to it alone. Start every single-leg set with the weak side and let its honest number set the load for both. Within a season the measurements converge, the knees quiet down, and your squat gains a foundation it was borrowing before. For a bodyweight athlete this work has one more gift: it loads the leg near its limit while the spine carries almost nothing, the safest heavy signal a hallway can produce.
Train with me, done-right depth. Four rounds, forty seconds of squats to the full depth you own, twenty seconds of rest. Range is the address. Deliver the whole order. Go.

beats.text: LOG DEPTH LIKE YOU LOG REPS

scenes.narration: Installation week. Anchor both leg days where nothing can move them. Write the two sessions into the log with a depth note for every squat set, because range unrecorded is range that quietly shrinks. Start every split squat with the weak side. Keep two reps in the tank so the week survives itself. The old way's habits to bury: the weekly destruction day that eats the following session. Quarter squats recorded as squats, a lie the log should never tell again. And calf work as a garnish, two rushed sets while putting shoes on. Done right is not more leg training than the old way. It is the same hours with the addresses corrected and the deliveries completed, which is why it works when the old way's greater suffering did not.

beats.text: THE BASE INTRODUCES ITSELF IN RATIOS

scenes.label: THEN WE MEASURE THE BASE AGAIN
scenes.narration: So, your ratio. Under zero point seven two: the old way wrote this, and the two anchored sessions are the single largest signal upgrade in your entire program. Zero point seven two to zero point eight zero: the build zone, where full range and frequency compound fastest on a light frame. Over zero point eight zero: the base stands up, keep the pillars and let the waist work widen the margin. Put your ratio in the comments, thigh divided by waist, just the number. In thirty days we measure both again, and the new ratio will show what legs do when every order finally arrives at the right address.
scenes.sub: old way / build zone / base built - range decides

scenes.narration: Log both numbers next to today's leg session. Thirty days from now we divide again, and the ratio will grade your range and frequency without caring about your intentions. If this helped, subscribe for the next test. This is {channel}. Train the cable.

title: Stop Doing skinny fat legs Wrong: Train Your leg muscle signals Instead
